title: fancy-sign: canonical JSON and the per-envelope hash-chained audit trail

contract.summary: One append-only chain per envelope, change-council's scheme with envelope_id in place of change_id. hash = sha256(prev_hash + "\n" + canonical({seq, envelope_id, at, type, actor, source, ip, user_agent, data})), genesis 64 zeros. Canonical JSON: keys sorted by UTF-8 byte order, recursively; list order kept; no whitespace; slashes, non-ASCII and U+2028/U+2029 unescaped; floats refused; empty data is the empty object. The event set is closed and only page.viewed may have source client. verify() reads raw rows and names the first problem: sequence_gap, broken_link or hash_mismatch. See SPEC.md.

functions.canonical: canonical(value, objects?) -> string | {error: "refused"}. `objects` lists the dot paths whose empty value is an OBJECT (a JSON decoder may not keep {} and [] apart).
functions.hash: hash(prev_hash, event) -> lowercase hex sha256. Missing ip, user_agent are null; missing data is {}.
functions.append: append(last | null, event) -> the stored event {envelope_id, seq, at, type, actor, source, ip, user_agent, data, prev_hash, hash} | {error: "refused"} for a type outside the closed set or a source the type may not have.
functions.verify: verify(rows) -> {ok, checked, head, seq?, problem?}. `data` may be an object or a JSON string.

contract.referenceNote: Goldens are particle-academy/fancy-sign's own output (EventChain, CanonicalJson), written by fancy-sign-php/tests/Conformance/Export.php; its DriftTest fails if a re-export moves a byte. Each row is run through a JSON round trip first, as a loader hands it over.

notes: tests/discrimination-sign.test.ts holds a faithful Node reading of SPEC.md and the mutants a port would plausibly be (UTF-16 key order, escaped slashes, [] for empty data, a missing broken_link check). Each mutant names the exact rows that catch it.
